newsitem.title: USA: White House forms working groups on tobacco deal.
newsitem.headline: White House forms working groups on tobacco deal.

text.p: President Clinton has formed eight working groups within his government to review the tobacco settlement and has given them 30 days to complete their analysis, the White House said Monday.

White House spokesman Barry Toiv told reporters the review had already begun and that a series of agencies were involved, including the Food and Drug Administration as well as the Justice, Treasury, Labour and Agriculture departments.
Briefing reporters during a presidential trip to San Francisco, Toiv said the first working group would cover the matter of FDA regulation as well as cigarette marketing, access and labeling issues.

A second group will study budget issues, examining how the money from the proposed $368.5 billion settlement would be spent, and a third would cover industry issues, including the industry's financial health and the incentives it would receive from the deal.
Toiv said the other five groups would cover workplace smoking; smoking cessation; litigation, liability and disclosure; international issues, and implementing the agreement.

Tobacco companies agreed on Friday to pay $368.5 billion, admit that tobacco is addictive and accept extensive federal regulation over their products and their advertising as part of a landmark agreement.

In return, the companies, which have never before been forced to pay for tobacco-related illnesses, would be given immunity from further punitive liability for deception, fraud or conspiracy that might have occurred in the past.
Clinton on Friday directed his chief domestic policy adviser Bruce Reed and Secretary of Health and Human Services Donna Shalala to coordinate the government review of the deal.
